what_happened: Research found the same false claim (empty/"no goals" from lean_goal treated as proof completion) restated in two additional surfaces beyond the dispatch's named gap: README.md:54 ("no goals" = done) and agents/lean-implementation-agent.md:753 ("Always verify proofs are actually complete (no goals)"). The dispatch's own grep covered absence of a caveat, not presence of the claim elsewhere. Flagged for planning to decide whether these should also point at the new canonical statement, kept out of this task's own edit scope pending that decision.

Planning closed the research report's one open evidentiary gap cheaply: a 4-line standalone Lean probe (theorem closed by 'exact <unknown constant>' plus '#print axioms') measured the synthetic-sorryAx mechanism directly on Lean 4.33.0-rc1 -- output 'depends on axioms: [sorryAx]' while the goal itself is closed. The caveat's causal claim is now measured in this repository rather than carried as standard-behavior assertion, so the plan can tag it with an evidentiary marker matching metadata-trust-surfaces.md's own convention instead of hedging.

validate-artifact.sh's advisory authoring-shape scan caught three real plan defects before the plan was committed: a Files-to-modify continuation line beginning with a backtick (silently read as prose rather than a second entry), a Tier Justification naming only 3 of the 18 suites suite_selection_select actually returns for the touched path, and two deployed .claude/** paths named as Files-to-modify entries for traceability (never legitimate file_scope members, and refused by plan-file-scope-harvest.sh). All three were fixed at authoring time; re-validation reports 0 warnings and the harvest yields exactly the four intended entries.
